why_there_is_no_record: The build failed, so there was nothing to measure. Every platform job in this tag's packaging run died on the same line of packaging/gigaxml.spec -- VERSION_TUPLE = tuple(int(part) for part in VERSION.split('.')[:4]) -- with ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '0rc1'. Linux, Windows and macOS failed identically, the release and Publish to PyPI jobs were skipped, the run uploaded no artifacts, and no Release exists for this tag. No sweep ran, so there is no run to point at and no figure to record.
why_this_is_the_first_tag_that_could_fai: Not the first time the pipeline ran -- nine earlier tag builds all succeeded on all three platforms. It is the first tag whose pyproject.toml actually carried a pre-release suffix. Every earlier build read a plain three-number version, including the rehearsal tags: v0.9.0rc1 and v0.9.0rc2 were cut from a tree whose pyproject.toml read 0.9.0, and v1.2.0rc1 and v1.2.0rc2 from one that read 1.2.0. A tag named for a pre-release that does not put the pre-release in the version the build reads is how nine green builds taught nothing about this line. int(part) had never been handed a non-digit before this tag.
the_defect_had_two_copies_and_only_one_w: packaging/gigaxml.iss and packaging/gigaxml.spec each reduce the version to the four integers a Windows version resource holds. The .iss copy was repaired in 10d6102, an ancestor of this tag: it now takes the digits from tools/make_version_info.py and keeps the readable AppVersion separate. The spec copy was not, and still split the string apart itself at this tag -- so the half that was tested shipped and the half that was not did not. The .iss comment had already named the shape of the trap when it was fixed ('a literal here was exactly the second copy of a number that will rot'), and the spec's own comment, written with the repair after this tag, says why the untested copy is the one that breaks: it is the copy nobody can see until a release build fails.
no_numbers_were_fabricated_here: Deliberately empty of numbers, and for a stronger reason than the entries before it: nothing was measured, not because a measurement was skipped but because no artifact was ever produced. Any figure here would describe a binary that does not exist.
what_would_close_this: The 2.0.0 release is where the measurement is taken, for the same reason 1.2.1.json gives. perf_baseline.py and run_comparison.py now write schema_version, an identity block, the generated dataset's seed and digest, and every individual run's raw values, so that record will be generated rather than reconstructed. The packaging half of this entry closes separately: e45ecbf, after this tag, pointed the spec at the same version_quad the installer asks and added tools/spec_check.py, which executes the spec on every pull request -- so the next bump to a pre-release goes red there rather than here.
